rule: The file has exactly 3 columns (Date, Description, Amount) or exactly 4 columns (Date, Description, Credit, Debit), in that order.
why_it_matters: QuickBooks Online only maps these two layouts; extra columns such as Balance or Reference make the upload fail or map wrong.

rule: In the 4-column layout the headers read Credit and Debit, without the word "amount".
why_it_matters: Intuit lists removing the word amount from these headers as a fix for upload errors.

rule: Zero values are removed and the cell is left blank.
why_it_matters: A 0.00 in the Debit column of a deposit row is a common cause of a failed upload, per Intuit.

rule: Every date uses one format for the whole file.
why_it_matters: A file that mixes 03/04/2026 and 2026-04-03 can't be read one way.

rule: The date cell holds only the date, with no weekday text such as "TUE".
why_it_matters: Intuit tells you to split weekday text out of the date column before uploading.

rule: The file is 350 KB or less.
why_it_matters: Intuit's manual upload article states the 350 KB limit. Split a long period into smaller date ranges.

rule: The file has 1,000 transaction lines or fewer.
why_it_matters: Intuit's manual upload article says up to 1,000 lines per upload.

rule: In the 3-column layout, money out is negative and money in is positive.
why_it_matters: Intuit's example: payments as -100.00, deposits as 200.00. A credit card file from the bank may have the signs reversed.

rule: The Description is text from the statement and not only a number.
why_it_matters: Intuit says to correct transactions that show numbers in the Description column.

rule: Amounts are digits with an optional minus sign and decimal point: no $, no thousands commas, no parentheses, no CR/DR suffix.
why_it_matters: This spec's rule. Symbols and parentheses are the usual reason an amount column reads as text in a spreadsheet or maps wrong on upload.

rule: In the 4-column layout, each row fills exactly one of Credit or Debit.
why_it_matters: This spec's rule. A row with both filled or both blank has no single direction.

rule: Every row has a date that exists on the calendar and falls inside the statement period when a header sidecar is given.
why_it_matters: This spec's rule. Catches 02/30 and rows carried over from the next statement.

rule: Opening balance plus the sum of the rows equals the printed closing balance when a header sidecar is given.
why_it_matters: This spec's rule. QuickBooks imports whatever rows you give it; a missed or doubled row only shows up later, when the reconciliation doesn't tie.

rule: No two rows share the same date
source: This spec's rule. Often a real repeat (two identical coffees) but often a page break read twice. Check it against the PDF.

rule: No summary rows: lines such as Opening balance, Closing balance, Total or Balance forward are not transactions.
why_it_matters: This spec's rule. A balance line imported as a transaction doubles the balance.
